sections.changelog:
Fixed

  • **Indexing no longer silently no-ops on clustered databases.** The per-object advisory lock treated "lock service unavailable" the same as "lock held by another writer" and skipped the write in both cases. On MySQL setups that do not provide user-level locks (Galera / Percona XtraDB Cluster and some managed or proxied hosts) `GET_LOCK` returns NULL rather than 1, so every index write was dropped and the index stayed empty. A NULL result now runs the write unlocked; a genuine conflict (another writer holds the lock) still skips, as intended.
  • **Manual and background reindex no longer fight each other.** After a schema upgrade the index rebuilds in the background; clicking "Reindex everything" while that was running started a second driver over the same cursor, so the two contended per object and the browser progress bar could stall (showing, for example, a stuck "500 of N" while the index read empty). The browser now holds a short lease while its tab drives the loop and the scheduled drain yields to it, so exactly one worker runs at a time — the tab while it is open, the cron once it closes.
